Long turn brief minutes
The training meeting was held in the Companion Animal Travel Desk at Aurelia Skyways. Attendance was noted by Nikhil Sato and Maya Kaur, with Phoebe mentioned during the welfare review.

The shift review focused on routine intake checks for cats and dogs traveling between skyports. The team agreed that comfort notes must be written clearly, with feeding, water, and carrier condition recorded before handoff to crews. The welfare coordinator reminded staff to watch for stress signs at reception and to pass along calm, plain instructions without delay. Several recent cases were discussed as examples of good practice, especially where travelers arrived early and paperwork was complete.

The desk also reviewed communication with flight crews. Staff agreed that short handover notes should highlight any special handling needs and that updates should be shared as soon as changes are confirmed. The group noted that clear language reduces confusion and helps maintain animal comfort through boarding and transit. Attention was given to keeping carrier labels visible and checking that every item matches the booking details.

The final discussion covered customer contact at the counter. The team agreed to stay brisk, polite, and consistent when explaining rules on carrier size, feeding gaps, and arrival steps. It was noted that travelers respond well when guidance is direct and repeated in the same order each time. No major issues were raised, and the desk will continue to reinforce the same routine checks on the next shift.
